fieldflow.name: FieldFlow
fieldflow.tagline: From field photos to structured service reports.
fieldflow.title: FieldFlow — turning field service paperwork into structured workflows
fieldflow.intro: Field technicians often share photos of completed service reports through messaging apps. Coordinators then spend time interpreting, organizing and forwarding those documents by hand. FieldFlow is a proposed AI-assisted workflow that would turn those scattered photos into structured, reviewable records.

spec.audienceValue: Field service operators, maintenance teams, operations managers, coordinators

challenge.heading: Important service data gets stuck in chat threads
challenge.body: After a site visit, a technician may photograph a paper protocol and send it through a messaging app. A coordinator must identify the job, read the document, re-enter key details, check for missing information and forward it to the right recipient. The process depends on manual hand-offs and makes tracking, retrieval and consistency harder as the volume of reports grows.

solution.heading: One place to capture, review and route field reports
solution.body: FieldFlow explores a mobile-friendly submission flow and a coordinator workspace. An AI document-processing step would suggest structured fields from uploaded photos. A human reviewer would confirm or correct those fields before generating a clean report and preparing it for delivery. The design keeps people in control of final approval.

steps.title: Capture
steps.body: A technician uploads one or more photos of a completed service protocol.

steps.title: Extract
steps.body: AI-assisted processing proposes key fields such as job reference, date, customer, work performed and notes.

steps.title: Review
steps.body: A coordinator checks the source image alongside the extracted information and corrects anything uncertain.

steps.title: Prepare & send
steps.body: Once approved, the workflow prepares a standardized PDF or structured export for authorized delivery.

value.heading: Designed to reduce repetitive coordination work
items: Less manual transcription and repetitive forwarding.
More consistent report structure and easier retrieval.
Clearer review and approval responsibilities.
Better visibility into outstanding or incomplete reports.
value.disclaimer: These are expected benefits of the proposed workflow, not validated results. No performance measurements are available yet.

principles.heading: Practical automation with human oversight
items: Mobile-first submission for technicians in the field.
Explicit human validation before external delivery.
Visibility into missing or low-confidence information.
Traceability from the original image to the final report.
Data protection and access controls as requirements for any future implementation.

nextSteps.heading: A concept today, a potential MVP next
nextSteps.body: FieldFlow is currently a solution concept. A future proof-of-concept implementation could validate document extraction accuracy, review time and coordinator usability using synthetic or properly authorized sample documents. No production deployment or customer results are claimed.

invoiceflow.name: InvoiceFlow
invoiceflow.tagline: Turn scattered invoices into a consistent approval process.
invoiceflow.title: InvoiceFlow — bringing supplier invoices into one reviewable approval flow
invoiceflow.intro: Supplier invoices often arrive across several inboxes as attachments, scans or paper copies. Someone then has to read each one, copy the key details and chase the right person for approval. InvoiceFlow is a proposed AI-assisted workflow that would collect incoming invoices in one place and guide them through a clear, human-approved process.

spec.audienceValue: Finance teams, accountants, small and mid-sized businesses, multi-location operations

challenge.heading: Invoices are spread across inboxes and attachments
challenge.body: Supplier invoices land in personal mailboxes, shared inboxes and sometimes on someone's desk. Employees manually extract the vendor, total, due date and cost center, then forward the document to whoever needs to approve it. Without a single overview, it is hard to tell which invoices are pending, where they are stuck and whether one has already been entered. As volume grows, due dates and audit questions become harder to manage.

solution.heading: One intake point and a clear path to approval
solution.body: InvoiceFlow explores a single intake point for supplier invoices and a simple approval workspace. An AI document-processing step would propose key fields from each invoice and flag possible duplicates or missing data. The responsible person would review, correct and approve the invoice before it is prepared as an export for accounting software. Accounting integrations, tax checks and fraud detection are treated as possible future capabilities, not guaranteed outcomes.

steps.title: Receive
steps.body: Invoices are forwarded to a dedicated address or uploaded directly into one shared queue.

steps.title: Extract
steps.body: AI-assisted processing proposes fields such as vendor, invoice number, total, due date and cost center.

steps.title: Check
steps.body: The workflow flags possible duplicates and missing or inconsistent data before anyone approves.

steps.title: Assign
steps.body: Each invoice is routed to an approval owner based on simple, agreed rules.

steps.title: Approve
steps.body: The approver compares the original document with the extracted fields and confirms or returns the invoice.

steps.title: Export
steps.body: Approved invoices are prepared as a structured export for accounting software.

value.heading: Designed to make invoice handling more predictable
items: More consistent intake from every channel.
Fewer copy-and-paste tasks between documents and spreadsheets.
A clearer audit trail of who reviewed and approved each invoice.
Better visibility into pending approvals and upcoming due dates.
Earlier detection of possible duplicates and missing details.
value.disclaimer: These are expected benefits of the proposed workflow, not validated results. No performance measurements are available yet.

principles.heading: Automation that keeps finance in control
items: Human approval before any invoice moves to accounting.
The original document always visible next to the extracted data.
Clear flags for duplicates, gaps and low-confidence fields.
Export for accounting software; direct connections to existing systems only in a future phase.
Data protection and role-based access as requirements for any future implementation.

quoteflow.name: QuoteFlow
quoteflow.tagline: Build consistent proposals without rebuilding spreadsheets.
quoteflow.title: QuoteFlow — consistent B2B quotes without rebuilding spreadsheets
quoteflow.intro: Many B2B sales teams still build each quote by copying rows between spreadsheets and adjusting prices by hand. Versions multiply, pricing rules live in people's heads and approvals happen over email. QuoteFlow is a proposed workflow that would guide quote preparation from template to an approved, versioned proposal.

spec.audienceValue: Manufacturers, installers, B2B sales teams, technical service providers

challenge.heading: Every quote starts with another spreadsheet copy
challenge.body: Salespeople copy line items from older quotes, look up current prices and manually apply discounts and margin rules. A small formula mistake can go unnoticed until the customer replies. When a manager needs to approve an exception, the request travels by email or chat, and the latest version is not always obvious. Tracking which proposals are open, revised or accepted gets harder as the team grows.

solution.heading: Templates, pricing rules and approvals in one flow
solution.body: QuoteFlow explores a quote builder based on templates and a shared catalog of items. Agreed pricing and margin rules would be applied consistently, and exceptions would be routed to a manager for approval. Each approved quote would be generated as a versioned PDF with a visible status. Connections to existing systems could be explored in a future phase; none are assumed today.

steps.title: Start
steps.body: Select the customer and a suitable quote template.

steps.title: Configure
steps.body: Add items from a shared catalog and set quantities or options.

steps.title: Price
steps.body: Approved pricing and margin rules are applied automatically and consistently.

steps.title: Approve exceptions
steps.body: Discounts or terms outside the rules go to a manager for approval.

steps.title: Generate
steps.body: The workflow produces a clean, versioned PDF proposal.

steps.title: Track
steps.body: Each proposal has a visible status: draft, sent, revised or accepted.

value.heading: Designed to make quoting faster and more consistent
items: Faster preparation of standard quotes.
Fewer formula and copy-and-paste mistakes.
Consistent pricing and approval rules across the team.
Traceable revisions and a clear history for every proposal.
Better overview of open and pending proposals.
value.disclaimer: These are expected benefits of the proposed workflow, not validated results. No performance measurements are available yet.

principles.heading: Structured sales work without losing flexibility
items: Templates and catalog as a single source for quote content.
Pricing rules agreed with the business, not hidden in formulas.
Manager approval for exceptions before a quote leaves the company.
Version history for every proposal.
Connection to existing systems only as a future, verified option.

nextSteps.body: QuoteFlow is currently a solution concept. A future proof-of-concept implementation could validate quote preparation time, pricing-rule coverage and usability for sales staff using synthetic or properly authorized sample data. No production deployment or customer results are claimed.

shiftflow.name: ShiftFlow
shiftflow.tagline: Replace chat-based timesheets with a reviewable reporting flow.
shiftflow.title: ShiftFlow — from chat-based timesheets to a reviewable reporting flow
shiftflow.intro: In many teams, hours worked are reported through messages and pieced together in spreadsheets at month-end. ShiftFlow is a proposed mobile workflow that would capture shifts as they happen and give supervisors a clear way to review them.

spec.audienceValue: Construction, logistics, production and field teams

challenge.heading: Hours are reported in messages and pieced together later
challenge.body: Employees send their hours through messaging apps, text messages or paper notes. At month-end, a manager consolidates everything into a spreadsheet and chases missing or unclear entries before payroll.

solution.heading: Simple mobile reporting with supervisor review
solution.body: ShiftFlow explores a mobile form for logging shifts against a job or site. Supervisors would review entries, resolve exceptions and prepare a payroll-ready export, so problems surface during the month rather than at its end.

steps.title: Submit
steps.body: Employees log their hours from a phone right after the shift.

steps.title: Associate
steps.body: Each entry is linked to a job, site or shift.

steps.title: Review
steps.body: A supervisor checks and confirms the submitted entries.

steps.title: Resolve
steps.body: Missing or unusual entries are flagged and clarified with the employee.

steps.title: Export
steps.body: Approved hours are prepared as a payroll-ready export.

value.heading: Designed to reduce month-end reconciliation
items: Fewer missing or unclear entries.
Less manual consolidation at month-end.
A clear record of who approved which hours.
value.disclaimer: These are expected benefits of the proposed workflow, not validated results. No performance measurements are available yet.

principles.heading: Easy for the team, clear for supervisors
items: Quick mobile entry that fits into a working day.
Supervisor review before anything reaches payroll.
Payroll-ready export; connection to existing systems only in a future phase.
Data protection and access controls as requirements for any future implementation.

nextSteps.body: ShiftFlow is currently a solution concept. A future proof-of-concept could validate ease of entry and review effort using synthetic or properly authorized sample data. No production deployment or customer results are claimed.

stockflow.name: StockFlow
stockflow.tagline: Make stock movements easier to capture and verify.
stockflow.title: StockFlow — lightweight visibility into stock movements
stockflow.intro: Smaller warehouses and retail teams often track stock changes in several spreadsheets that rarely match. StockFlow is a proposed lightweight workflow that would make every stock movement quick to record and easy to verify.

spec.audienceValue: Warehouses, distributors, small retail and e-commerce teams

challenge.heading: Stock changes live in separate spreadsheets
challenge.body: Receipts, transfers and adjustments are recorded by different people in different files, often after the fact. Reconciling them takes time, and it is hard to say which number is current or who made a change.

solution.heading: Record each movement once, see it everywhere
solution.body: StockFlow explores scanning an item or QR code on a phone to record a movement with its quantity and location. Each change would be validated and reflected in a shared view, with notifications when stock crosses thresholds the team sets.

steps.title: Scan
steps.body: Scan an item or QR code with a phone.

steps.title: Record
steps.body: Enter the movement: receipt, transfer, issue or adjustment.

steps.title: Validate
steps.body: Quantity and location are checked before the change is saved.

steps.title: Update
steps.body: The shared stock view updates for the whole team.

steps.title: Notify
steps.body: The team is notified when stock crosses a configured threshold.

value.heading: Designed for more timely stock visibility
items: A more timely view of current stock levels.
Traceable adjustments with a clear author and time.
Fewer manual hand-offs between spreadsheets.
value.disclaimer: These are expected benefits of the proposed workflow, not validated results. No performance measurements are available yet.

principles.heading: Lightweight by design
items: Fast capture on a phone, right where the stock is.
Validation at entry rather than reconciliation later.
A clear history for every adjustment.
Connection to existing systems only in a future phase.

nextSteps.heading: A concept today, a potential MVP next
nextSteps.body: StockFlow is currently a solution concept. A future proof-of-concept could validate capture speed and data consistency using synthetic or properly authorized sample data. No production deployment or customer results are claimed.

fixflow.name: FixFlow
fixflow.tagline: From scattered maintenance messages to accountable requests.
fixflow.title: FixFlow — from scattered maintenance messages to accountable requests
fixflow.intro: Maintenance requests often arrive by phone and email, and it is easy to lose track of who is handling what. FixFlow is a proposed workflow that would turn each request into a tracked task with a clear owner, from report to resolution.

spec.audienceValue: Property managers, facility teams, multi-site operators

challenge.heading: Requests arrive from everywhere, ownership is unclear
challenge.body: Tenants, staff and site managers report issues by phone and email. Coordinators lack a reliable overview of which requests are open, who owns them and whether they were actually resolved.

solution.heading: One request, one owner, one history
solution.body: FixFlow explores a simple submission form with photos, followed by classification, prioritization and assignment to a technician. Updates would be tracked in one place, and a coordinator would review completion before closing the request.

steps.title: Submit
steps.body: The reporter describes the issue and attaches a photo.

steps.title: Classify
steps.body: The request is categorized and given a priority.

steps.title: Assign
steps.body: A technician or contractor is assigned as the owner.

steps.title: Track
steps.body: Progress updates are recorded on the request.

steps.title: Close
steps.body: A coordinator reviews completion and closes the request.

value.heading: Designed for clearer accountability
items: Clearer ownership of every request.
A searchable history of issues and repairs.
Fewer missed follow-ups.
value.disclaimer: These are expected benefits of the proposed workflow, not validated results. No performance measurements are available yet.

principles.heading: Simple to report, clear to manage
items: Quick reporting with a photo.
Every request has exactly one current owner.
Coordinator review before a request is closed.
Data protection and access controls as requirements for any future implementation.
